text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- State Bank governor Cao Si Kiem has affirmed there will be no devaluation of the dong.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has agreed in principle that Cat Bi airport in Haiphong should be upgraded to international status.
-- The Trade Ministry plans to increase annual export turnover to $12 billion by 2000.
-- The Ho Chi Minh City Economics Court has issued its first bankruptcy ruling against Duc Thang Ltd, a garment trading company.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet is due to begin a friendship visit to India and Bangladesh.
-- Seventeen percent of Vietnam's 6,250 state-owned enterprises are operating at a loss.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has urged improvements to the country's education system.
-- Twenty percent of private businesses in Ho Chi Minh City are operating at a loss.
-- The Labour, War Invalids and Social Affairs Ministry is considering proposals to reduce the working week in Vietnam to five and a half days, from six.
